To test robustness against this instability and capture diverse information from the full pool without overfitting to recent noise, I will test a simple mean over the entire model pool, which serves as a strong baseline for diversity-based combination.

The current leader (a7) uses a trimmed mean on a small top-3 pool (ETS, FT_rf, FT_catboost). To test robustness against this specific "robust" approach in an unstable ranking regime (ranking_tau=0.072), I will use the newly created pool8 (top 5 by RMSE: ETS, FT_rf, FT_catboost, ARIMA, catboost) and apply a simple mean combination. This tests if including slightly less accurate but complementary models (ARIMA, catboost) helps stabilize the forecast without the trimming.

The current leader (a7) uses a trimmed mean on the top-3 models. To test if robust aggregation on the full pool can overcome the unstable ranking, I will evaluate DBA on the full pool, which minimizes variance more aggressively than a standard mean while being less sensitive to outliers than a simple mean.

The series has strong trend and seasonality but unstable ranking (ranking_tau=0.072), suggesting that simple robust combinations like DBA or trimmed mean are effective. However, the leader (DBA) is only slightly better than the runner-up, and given the low predictability and noise-dominated spectrum, a weighted combination using inverse error weights on the full pool might better leverage the diverse strengths of the top performers without being overly sensitive to any single model's recent instability.

The DBA leader (a10) leverages robustness against ranking instability, a key feature here (tau=0.072). However, DBA can be sensitive to outliers or specific window configurations. I want to test if a simple Trimmed Mean on the full pool provides similar robustness with less complexity, potentially offering a better bias-variance tradeoff for this noisy, stationary series.
